## Conclusion

I present evidence of a non-detectable shift in the
clock hour of daily maximum temperature at Épinal, France, over the
1986--2025 period, estimated using a von Mises circular regression
framework with bootstrap uncertainty quantification. The estimated trend
of $-0.0281$ h/decade is consistent with the global
phase shifts reported by Shmuel et al. [-@shmuel2026daily] and the
European diurnal cycle changes documented by Wang and
Dillon [-@wang2014recent].

The trend remains robust across eight pre-registered
sensitivity variants, suggesting that the result is not an artefact of
specific methodological choices. A year--season interaction
likelihood-ratio test was significant ($\chi^2 = 13.71$, df = 3,
$p = 0.0033$), supporting per-season inference with
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Winter shows a significant advance of
$-0.19$ h/decade ($p = 0.0015$), while spring, summer, and autumn do
not show significant trends after correction.

These findings contribute local-scale, station-level evidence to the
emerging picture of a changing diurnal temperature phase. Replication
across the broader Météo-France RADOME network and extension to
other regions with long sub-daily temperature records are natural next
steps. If the shift is confirmed more broadly, it would warrant
re-evaluation of applied models -- from heat-health warning systems to
building energy and crop modelling -- that currently assume a stationary
diurnal cycle.

**Data and code availability.** All analysis code is available at
[https://github.com/Ron-RONZZ-org/epinal-diurnal-peak-temperature](
https://github.com/Ron-RONZZ-org/epinal-diurnal-peak-temperature).
Raw temperature data were obtained from the Météo-France public
API. Processed data and the pre-registration are archived on OSF
(DOI to be assigned upon submission).
